tutorial.actionHint: A checklist that builds the HungerStation against QC report, ticking each step as you do it
tutorial.title: Build the HungerStation against QC report
tutorial.finished: Done. This is a report your team can re-run for any period. Save it, then share and schedule it from its page.
tutorial.loadHint: Skip to the end and study it. Undo takes you back to where you were.
tutorial.askHow: Type this sentence to the copilot and it builds the whole report, which opens here:
tutorial.sentence: How were sales for each channel yesterday? Focus on two order types, HungerStation and QC, compare them, and show their cancellation rates. The period is a parameter that defaults to yesterday and can be changed. Save it as a report template my team can re-run, schedule it every day by email to named people, and include charts.

title.title: Name the report
title.how: Type a title above the page, e.g. "Channel sales: HungerStation against QC". One language is enough.

section.title: Add a section
section.how: Use "Add a section" and call it "Sales by channel". Sections are read top to bottom.

chart.title: Chart net sales by channel
chart.how: In the section, use "Add to this section", then "Chart or table". Pick the value through our tills, break it down by channel, and choose bars.

series.title: Compare HungerStation against QC
series.how: Add another chart, then two named series: one where the channel is HungerStation, one where the delivery type is QC. Each series runs on its own.

rate.title: Show their cancellation rates
rate.how: On a chart with those two series, pick the Orders area and its cancellation rate, by day.

figure.title: Write a sentence with a live figure
figure.how: Add Text and use "Insert a live figure" to drop in, say, HungerStation’s rate. It is filled in on every run.

summary.title: Add the AI summary
summary.how: Add "AI summary" to a last section. It is rewritten on every run and its numbers are checked.

period.title: The period: yesterday, on every chart
period.how: Every new report has a Period parameter. Set its default to Yesterday in the strip above the page, and check that "Applies to" ticks every chart (open it from the outline).

sqlEditor.needsTitle: Give it a title to save it.

sqlEditor.runFailed: The statement could not be run

reason.not-parsed: The statement could not be read as SQL.
reason.not-one-select: Only one SELECT statement can be run.
reason.table-not-allowed: The statement reads a table that is not open to SQL.
reason.column-not-allowed: The statement reads a column that is not open to SQL.
reason.join-not-on-list: The statement joins tables in a way that is not allowed.
reason.facts-not-grouped: Rows from a facts table must be grouped (summed or counted), not listed one by one.
reason.function-not-allowed: The statement uses a function that is not allowed.
reason.busy: Too many statements are running. Try again in a moment.
reason.timed-out: The statement took too long and was stopped.
reason.not-available: SQL is not available right now.
reason.needs-sql-grant: Running SQL needs the SQL grant.
